title: He didn’t heal him in public.
paragraphs: He didn’t heal him in public.

No stage.
No applause.
No crowd to impress.

Just Jesus…
and a broken man…
in a quiet place.
That’s how Mark 7:33–35 unfolds.

A man who could not hear.
A man who could barely speak.
A man trapped inside his own silence.
And Jesus does something unexpected—He takes him away from the noise.
Why?

Because some miracles are too intimate for the crowd.
Some healings are not for display… but for restoration.

He touches his ears.
He touches his tongue.
He looks up to heaven and sighs—
then speaks one word:

“Ephphatha.”
Be opened.
And instantly… everything changes.

Ears that never heard… open.
A tongue that struggled… loosens.
A life that felt locked… is released.
Because this is not just his story.
This is ours.
Sin has a way of closing things.

Closing ears to truth.
Closing mouths that should speak life.
Closing hearts that once burned for God.

You can sit in church… and still be deaf.
You can know the language… and still be mute in your spirit.
You can look alive… but feel shut down inside.

And here’s the dangerous part—
we get used to it.

We normalize the silence.
We adjust to the numbness.
We learn to function… without hearing God clearly anymore.
But Jesus doesn’t leave people that way.

He doesn’t shout from a distance.
He doesn’t heal mechanically.
He comes close.

Personal.
Intentional.
Compassionate.
He touches the very places we hide.

The ears we’ve closed.
The voice we’ve silenced.
The heart we’ve hardened.
And then He speaks.

Not just information…
but transformation.
“Be opened.”

That’s not just a command.
That’s resurrection power in one sentence.
But here’s what we often miss…

Before the opening…
there is surrender.

The man didn’t argue.
He didn’t resist.
He allowed Jesus to lead him away.

Away from the crowd.
Away from distractions.
Away from everything familiar.
And that’s where many of us struggle.

We want public miracles…
but avoid private surrender.

We want healing…
without intimacy.

We want God to move…
but only on our terms.
But Jesus still works this way.
He still calls people aside.

Into prayer.
Into stillness.
Into that quiet, uncomfortable space
where it’s just you… and Him.
Because that’s where real change happens.
And don’t miss the bigger picture…

The same Jesus who opened deaf ears…
would soon stretch out His hands on a cross.

The same voice that said “Be opened”…
would cry, “It is finished.”
Why?
Because our deepest problem was never just physical.
It was spiritual.

We weren’t just deaf…
we were dead in sin.

Separated from God.
Unable to hear Him.
Unable to respond.

But through the cross—
through the blood of Jesus—
the way back is opened.

Forgiveness is opened.
New life is opened.
A restored relationship with God is opened.
This is the Gospel.

Not self-improvement.
Not behavior modification.
Resurrection.
So maybe this is your moment.

Maybe your ears have grown dull.
Maybe your voice has gone silent.
Maybe your heart feels locked again.
Then hear this…

Jesus is still saying,
“Be opened.”

Not tomorrow.
Not when you’re ready.
Now.

Bring Him your numbness.
Bring Him your silence.
Bring Him the parts of you that feel shut down.
Let Him touch what you’ve been hiding.
Let Him lead you away from the noise.
Let Him speak.

And when He does…
everything changes.
If this stirred something in you, don’t ignore it.
Because Jesus is still opening what sin tried to shut.
And what He opens…
no darkness can ever close.
